prompt: Write a reusable equals-and-hash helper that compares only the fields marked @Identity, whatever the class. Complete the starter file, then run the tests.
explanation: Hand-written equals and hashCode drift out of sync with the fields they cover; driving both from one annotation keeps them consistent by construction. Comparing a.getClass() != b.getClass() first is what makes the helper safe across unrelated types, and it also guarantees the two objects declare the same @Identity fields. Objects.equals handles null values on either side without extra branching, and Objects.hash over the same values in the same order satisfies the contract that equal objects must share a hash code. The pattern only works because @Identity is declared with RUNTIME retention.
hints: Both methods share the same shape: loop over getDeclaredFields(), skip anything where isAnnotationPresent(Identity.class) is false, then setAccessible(true) before reading.
In sameIdentity, return false as soon as one pair of values differs; only after the whole loop finishes can you return true.
For the hash, gather the values into a List<Object> and finish with Objects.hash(values.toArray()) -- that spreads the list across the varargs parameter.
